title: Quarterly compatibility sprint: liaison plan and SLA margining for Private/VPC/On‑Prem
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Goal: Run a focused quarter-long compatibility sprint that aligns Product, Engineering, Design, and Customer Success to shrink unknowns for Private/VPC/On‑Prem deployments. Deliver a validated interop checklist, updated SLA margin recommendations, and a liaison cadence for high-touch enterprise customers. Scope includes: compatibility matrix updates for supported OS/container runtimes, networking guide for common VPC topologies, upgrade fencing and rollback policies, and an SLA margining playbook that maps SLOs to reserve capacity and autoscale policies. Out of scope: new model formats or major runtime refactors; these will be handled in separate platform epics.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix updated with test results for top 12 customer configurations
SLA margining playbook published with quantified reserve targets and example calculations
Runbook for interop-gateway misconfigurations (network, DNS, MTU) with remediation steps
Design sign-off for on‑prem installer pack and VPC quickstart networking templates
Customer liaison calendar created and two pilot customers scheduled for guided rollout
plan_summary: Week 1–2: discovery with CSMs and field engineers to collect top failure modes. Week 3–6: engineering test runs across prioritized infra shapes, parallel docs and runbook drafts. Week 7–9: design & UX iterate on private console onboarding flows and installer prompts. Week 10–12: pilot rollouts with two customers, gather telemetry, compute SLA margin statistics; finalize playbook and ship to docs and solutions templates.
risks: Test harness may not cover obscure customer kernel versions leading to late compatibility findings
Pilot customers could surface infra issues that require cross-team scheduling (storage/network)
Resource contention with runtime performance sprint (ENG-33877) could delay test completion
Security review gating (third‑party installer components) may add a 2+ week hold if not triaged early
mitigations: Prioritize top 5 OS/kernel variants based on customer telemetry and iterate on remaining in follow-up
Book cross-functional strike team sessions twice weekly during pilot window
Allocate a dedicated QA runner and isolated CI pool for compatibility tests
Early security sync with SRE and Security on week 1 to pre-clear third‑party packaging
